fda510kStageProgress.reason: ADJUDICATED 2026-09-06 (ledger L173) — CONFIRMED WRITERLESS AND HARMFUL, kept declared. fda_510k_stage_progress has no INSERT anywhere in server/ or the migrations; the only one in the repository is in a test fixture. Its single UPDATE, SmartFieldLinking.updateWorkflowField, is guarded by `if (progress.length > 0)` on a SELECT of this table, so on any deployment it is a silent no-op and EVERY `source: 'document'` field update is dropped. The harm was not the empty read but what the callers said about it: updateField returned Promise<void>, so POST /api/field-sync/update-field answered "Field updated and synchronized" unconditionally and the socket handler emitted field-update-success AND broadcast field-updated to every subscriber in the project room — putting a value on other clients' screens that the database never held. FIXED at the honesty boundary: updateField now returns applied | not-linked | no-destination | failed, the route answers 409 NO_DESTINATION_ROW instead of success, and the broadcast fires only when a row actually took the value. The store stays declared here because giving it a writer is a FEATURE (provisioning 510(k) stage rows), not a repair, and inventing one unasked would be a shape change; what is fixed is that its emptiness can no longer be reported as a successful save.

protocols.reason: ADJUDICATED 2026-09-05 (ledger L167): `protocols` has NO insert anywhere in the repo — not in server code, not in migrations, not even a seed — so it is empty on every deployment. Its one UPDATE (protocol-analyzer-service.ts:422) writes an embedding cache onto a row it just read, so it is empty-by-construction rather than an independent writer. Two consumers: findSimilarProtocols, which therefore always returns [], and strategic-report-generator, which has no callers and already fails closed ('Protocol not found'). The empty read is NOT correct — but the harm sits in the consumer, not here: POST /api/analytics/demo-analysis renders the always-zero count into a wisdom_trace 'Evidence Base' as "Compared against database of 0 similar protocols". See L167 for that and for the gate hole around it.

qSubCommitments.reason: ADJUDICATED 2026-09-05 (ledger L166): the capture half of the Pre-Sub cycle is unbuilt. The only mutation anywhere in product code is setCommitmentRolledIn (q-sub.service.ts), exposed as PATCH /api/q-sub/commitments/:id/rolled-in and as the AnA tool update_q_sub_commitment_rolled_in — both UPDATE-by-id, so on any real tenant they can never match a row. The only INSERT INTO q_sub_commitments is scripts/seed-mdx-beta.mjs, a beta seed, which is not a writer. AnA's own W3 Pre-Sub workflow instructs the user to "record their answer and capture commitments", a step the product provides no control for. So an empty read is NOT correct — it is a missing feature, and the readers see an empty set for that reason. Downstream: proposeCommitmentRollup has no callers, and the Pre-Sub Manager renders an honest "No commitments yet". Build the capture path or retire the cycle — a product call, recorded not made.

standardsApplicability.reason: ADJUDICATED 2026-09-06 (ledger L165) — CONFIRMED WRITERLESS, kept declared. `standards_applicability` has no INSERT anywhere in the repository, so listProgramApplicability returns nothing for every program. The harm was the reporting built on it: applicabilityGapReport filtered its non-conformant and missing-evidence counts from those rows and so reported ZERO of each — an empty store rendered as a clean standards assessment. FIXED in L165: the report now carries `assessed`, and nonConformantCount / missingEvidenceCount are null rather than 0 when nothing was examined, so 'nothing was assessed' can no longer be read as 'nothing was wrong'. The store stays declared because giving it a writer is a feature (building the applicability capture path), not a repair. Reason corrected 2026-09-06: L165 landed the fix but left this entry reading NOT ADJUDICATED, so the ledger and this baseline disagreed and the store kept appearing in the awaiting-a-decision list.
